Design & checks

Two 3 mm printed shells form a 60 mm deep closed backbone. Continuous side keys and eight M4 seam bolts join the shells. A 12 mm raised socket on the deck supports the root; four transverse M4 bolts clamp it. The 31 mm actuator grid and motor/controller locations are retained. The replacement structure uses 43.2% less solid CAD volume than the rear-braced version; all 24 assembly prints fit the H2S dimensional envelope with a 4 mm bed margin.

Print the front and rear trays with their broad outer faces down. The socket deck prints flat underside down. Download the three replacement parts above; retain the actuator, ring, fixed base and stand from the rigid-base kit. The STEP download contains the replacement structure and its fasteners.

The current ring is 224 mm across. Doubling it would be 448 mm and would not fit flat on an H2S. A possible future one-piece enlargement is a 296 mm ring with 264 teeth and a roughly 312 mm base, giving 22:1 with the 12T pinion. That enlargement is a sizing proposal, not the geometry shown here. H2S build volume: 340 × 320 × 340 mm.

The explosion separates service modules; the closed backbone stays assembled. Material comparison uses solid CAD volume, not slicer weight. Stiffness, creep and fit require printed tests. Four-arm swept clearance remains to be evaluated.
